scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports total network loss: they
cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2), and they cannot even ping their own
gateway 195.11.14.1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up. The
partner AS is healthy internally: pc2 reaches its gateway
200.1.1.1 fine. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the LAN interface (eth1) toward pc1 on router1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 eth1 (195.11.14.1/24, the LAN
  interface toward pc1)
Mechanism: router1's eth1 is DOWN, so pc1's only gateway address
  195.11.14.1 is gone from the segment -- pc1 cannot even ARP its
  gateway and loses all off-host connectivity. On router1 the
  connected route 195.11.14.0/24 disappears from the RIB, so the
  `network 195.11.14.0/24` statement has no matching route and
  the prefix is withdrawn from BGP -- AS 2 also loses its path to
  pc1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up (its side of the virtual
  segment is unaffected), which is why a host-side check looks
  clean. The inter-AS link and the eBGP session machinery are not
  the fault; the failure sits on the router1<->pc1 LAN leg.
Localization: router1
Root cause: router1 eth1 (LAN link to pc1) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth1 up` on router1
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth1 up` on router1. The gateway 195.11.14.1 comes back on the
segment, the connected route returns and BGP re-advertises 195.11.14.0/24
automatically; pc1 reaches pc2 normally. pc1 needs no change.

bonus-rules-out-host: notes pc1's own link/IP/route are intact; the failure is on router1's side of the segment

agent.diagnosis_text:
Router1's eth1 interface (195.11.14.1/24), which is the directly-connected
gateway for pc1, has been administratively shut down. The interface flags show
<BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no IFF_UP bit set, kernel state is DOWN, and
ethtool confirms "Link detected: no". This is an explicit administrative
shutdown (equivalent to `ip link set eth1 down`) rather than a physical cable
or hardware fault — pc1's own eth0 remains UP/LOWER_UP and the veth peer is
electrically present.

Because the interface is down, the kernel removes the connected route
195.11.14.0/24 from the routing table. FRR's BGP `network 195.11.14.0/24`
statement depends on that connected route being present in the RIB; with it
gone, FRR withdraws the advertisement to AS2 as well. This causes a cascade:
pc1 cannot ARP for its gateway (the interface won't process frames), so it
cannot reach 195.11.14.1 at all — explaining the reported "cannot ping own
gateway" symptom. All cross-AS reachability to pc2 is also lost as a secondary
effect. The BGP session itself (over eth0, 193.10.11.0/24) remains fully
established and router2/pc2 are unaffected.

Root cause: router1's eth1 was brought administratively down, severing pc1
from its gateway and withdrawing the 195.11.14.0/24 prefix from BGP.

Corrective fix: on router1, run `ip link set eth1 up`. The connected route will
re-appear in the RIB within seconds, FRR will re-advertise 195.11.14.0/24 to
router2 via BGP, and pc1's full connectivity will be restored.
